Each coefficient in the positive mixture is nonzero, so each row is carried by the sampled union and is absolutely continuous with respect to mixed d-volume. For every active plane at the source, affine barycenter equality and the L equality force its nonnegative gap to vanish row-almost everywhere. Distinct continuous gradients would confine the row to one hyperplane per fiber, a mixed-null set, contradicting probability one. At the target, finitely many distinct-gradient tie planes are also mixed-null. Ties between equal continuous gradients, including base-only ties on whole fibers, leave the derivative unchanged.

The active plane majorizes positive L on the source ball. Its value at the far endpoint in the direction opposite its gradient is L_i−r_s||c_i||, nonnegative by continuity even for an open ball. The bound is automatic for c_i=0. Integrating ||grad_X L|| against dm/(ML) via the mixture produces exactly M^(-1) times the volume integral of ||grad_X log L||.

Log normalization gives equal integrals of its positive and negative parts and forces L_max≥1, so the volume absolute-log constant is 2M log L_max. Positivity on the compact hull and the global finite affine formula give a positive neighborhood and hence Lipschitz log and absolute log there.

For the outward normal at an almost-everywhere regular boundary point, the supporting hyperplane and the inball imply n·(X−o_z)≥r_b. Both X and o_z lie in R B_d, giving ||X−o_z||≤2R. The weak product and chain rules give the divergence bound d|log L|+2R||grad_X log L||, including where log L vanishes. Gauss–Green on each positive convex body and summation give exactly 2dM log L_max/r_b+2RM/(r_b r_s). In d=1 the outward signs at the two endpoints give the same inequality by the interval fundamental theorem.
